reviews.title: App downgrade
reviews.text: Sweatcoin used to be a decent app that would track your steps fairly accurately. Now there are so many pop ups when you open the app it is ridiculous. There is a button feature that will count your steps for 20 minutes at 2x the points. I’ve noticed that when I don’t have the app open when the 20 minute timer runs down, the steps sometimes don’t get captured. This happens more often when you hit the button a second time for another 20 minutes. The app has moved away from what it was promoted as, a step counter app, to a wacky app with too many features and pop ups.

reviews.title: Too low sweepstake winning chance - deleted my account
reviews.text: Good app for tracking steps - bad app for winning prizes. Same as with Macadam and WeWard mostly only bots are winning the sweepstakes which have a human person giving commands in the back. Sure, it’s not so difficult to set up or develop a bot in JavaScript or C++/C# that just farms the game rewards and joins every competition autonomously. Or on jailbroken devices. But it sucks for people not being in the mood for learning to program and not having the time to play dozens of games and invest real money to increase the chances. The way those step reward apps work is the company behind the app has several partners with special offers such as games or products on sale. If a customer plays or purchases content the company and its partners receive money while the customer/user receives virtual worthless funds that can be exchanged to real rewards. However those apps are based solely on advertisements and marketing strategies thus the sweepstakes don’t offer fair competitions. The user with the highest amount spent on entry tickets wins. That’s totally waste of time and basically as if you’d buy all lottery tickets at your local lottery shop. People (including me) can earn way, WAY more money by creating and uploading erotic content on several adult content websites than using a step counting app which has its main focus on advertisement and partner product distribution. And from that earnings you can buy everything the Sweatcoin offers in their sweepstakes + make a living from.

reviews.title: I’ve had this app for years and…
reviews.text:
This app has remained open daily on my phone for the past 8 years. Over that time, I have earned a total of 5,966 sweatcoins and spent maybe a couple hundred sweatcoins total for random discounts (some of which were really good, I’ll admit) rather than actual “prizes”. That was probably 6 years ago? The actual prizes and discounts have been gotten rid of from the app. In order to get ANYTHING other than be in a raffle that you’ll never win, you need to have 15k or more sweatcoins. 

Today’s “prize” is a plastic water bottle that you can’t even see the actua price of unless you have 5,000 sweatcoins in the bank. Almost 8 years of walking and I can’t even afford a branded bad plastic water bottle because the app removed 1000 sweatcoins from my app last year without warning and their customer support has done nothing about it. 

Long story short, take it from me that this app is worthless now. Maybe 6 years ago it was fine, but it will never go back to having real prizes or actual good discounts. Today marks the day I finally delete the Sweatcoin app. I’m more excited to not have an app constantly open on my phone than I am for any prize this app could offer me.

reviews.title: Taugt auch ohne Geschenke zur Motivation
reviews.text: Das Negative gleich vorweg: Die Preise kann man meiner Meinung nach komplett vergessen. Gutscheine die was taugen sind immer ausverkauft, der Rest sind Coupons um an Daten oder Nutzer zu gelangen oder oft einfach Schrott. Ob die Spenden geleistet werden, kann ich nicht beurteilen. Macht aber nichts. Mich motiviert die schön programmierte App einfach nur, mich jeden Tag zu bewegen und damit Punkte und SWEATCOINS zu sammeln. Oft geh ich abends einfach nochmal eine Runde laufen, nur um die Punkte für den Boost zu bekommen. Allein dafür lohnen sich Account und App, zumindest für mich. Wenn dann doch irgendwann mal was anderes dabei rauskommen sollte auch okay. Geschenkt gibt es nichts, das sollte allen Nutzern der App bewusst sein.

reviews.title: 30.000 Schritte und nur 6.000 angezeigt
reviews.text:
Keine Ahnung, was da schief gelaufen ist aber ich gehe täglich mindestens 8.300 Schritte und die App zählt nicht einmal 6.000 und behauptet ich hätte seit Wochen keinen streak. Habe ein Fitnessarmband seit Monaten und mir werden hier coins unterschlagen.
Und warum so viel Werbung, wenn schon unsere Daten gesammelt werden.
